_status: DRAFT — newly proposed character wording for author review. Not manuscript text. Shown in the ship with a visible ‘Draft’ mark; remove or edit freely.
_guidance: Iri’s discipline shows in precision and care, never in diagnostic labels.
B.O.B. speaks only to what his sensors and logs could know; he does not claim private events.
Nova notices sound, structure and counts; she does not infer private relationships.

helm.quenby: The helm knows my hands. I don’t make speeches about it.
helm.iri: She sits forward when she’s working something out and back when she’s decided. From the auxiliary station I can see which.
helm.nova: Press the console edge and the deck answers a little late. Everything up here has a delay you can count.
helm.bob: Helm inputs are logged. Who sat here, and why, is not something my sensors record.

glass.quenby: Real glass. No display pretending to be a window. I’d rather know what’s actually out there.
glass.iri: The glass holds the cold longer than the bulkheads. I stand a step back from it.
glass.nova: Breathe on it and the stars go soft, then come back one at a time.
glass.bob: Forward glass: no faults. I keep the bridge lights low so it shows the dark instead of the room.

navlocks.quenby: Levers, not menus. You can find them in the dark, and I have.
navlocks.iri: Three levers. I know their positions by the sound they make seating.
navlocks.nova: Click, click, click. The last one is the loudest.
navlocks.bob: Course-hold engagement is logged by lever position. The levers do not ask me first.

copilot.quenby: Nobody was assigned that chair. People sit there anyway.
copilot.iri: The chair is left turned toward the hatch more often than not. I turn it back when I pass.
copilot.nova: It creaks on the left armrest. Only the left.
copilot.bob: This chair carries no seat sensor in my current records.

aux.quenby: The aux station sat empty a long time. I got used to talking past it.
aux.iri: I could draw the reach of every station on this bridge from memory. This one I could draw with my eyes shut.
aux.nova: The amber strip lights when somebody’s there. It stays lit a moment after they go.
aux.bob: The occupancy strip lights when the seat takes weight. It cannot tell me whose.

bolts.quenby: They migrate. I’ve stopped asking how.
bolts.iri: I step around them. Not because I’d trip. Because they’re arranged.
bolts.nova: If one’s missing, check the copilot cushion.
bolts.bob: Loose fasteners on the deck. I flagged them as a trip hazard once. The flag was dismissed.

rail.quenby: Worn smooth by somebody before me. I add to it.
rail.iri: The rail is load-rated for a hard burn. I check the brackets anyway.
rail.nova: Tap the rail and the whole bridge rings for a second. Quietly.
rail.bob: Rail indicators: green. They mean the station circuits are live, nothing more.

vbench.quenby: Bench by the glass. Good for sitting when you don’t want to be at the helm but can’t leave.
vbench.iri: The floor beside it is wide enough to lay a kit out flat. I have.
vbench.nova: From the bench you can see the glass and the hatch at once.
vbench.bob: The bench has no sensors. I hear it through the deck plating when it takes weight.

elbow.quenby: Halfway to the galley there’s the turn. I used to stop there for no reason I’d admit.
elbow.iri: The corridor jogs here. You hear someone coming before you see them.
elbow.nova: The hum changes at each bulkhead. Walk slowly and it’s a tune.
elbow.bob: Corridor plating registers footfall weight, not identity. I can tell you the corridor is used. I am careful not to say by whom.

powerpanel.quenby: Pull panel. If the lights stutter, this is where you start.
powerpanel.iri: Labels on the breakers are in three hands. I’ve learned all three.
powerpanel.nova: Put your ear near it and you can hear the bus settle.
powerpanel.bob: Distribution panel: within limits. I report the panel, not the people who open it.

counter.quenby: One long run. The prep end used to be mine by default. Now it’s mine when nobody else needs it.
counter.iri: The counter is built to her height and a hand too high for mine. I’ve stopped minding which of us it was built for.
counter.nova: The sink light blinks slower than a heartbeat. I matched it once.
counter.bob: Water draw at this sink is metered. I have no record of who taped the card above it.

tins.quenby: Somebody else’s handwriting on the labels. I keep them.
tins.iri: Three tins. I open the one that’s mine to open.
tins.nova: The middle tin rattles different. Not empty. Different.
tins.bob: I do not inventory the shelf. It has not shifted since the last hard burn.

heater.quenby: It hums off-key. B.O.B. calls that character. I have other words.
heater.iri: When it clicks off you feel it in the deck before you hear it.
heater.nova: Hum, hum, click. Every cycle. When it skips, everybody looks up.
heater.bob: Heater cycle completes with an audible click. I could correct the misaligned note. I have chosen not to.

cooler.quenby: Low and aft. Nobody designs a galley for knees.
cooler.iri: I check the seals by touch. The left gasket is older than the right.
cooler.nova: It shivers when it starts. Sit still on the bench and you feel it.
cooler.bob: Cold storage is holding temperature. I know its contents only as they are logged in, which is not always.

table.quenby: A real table. You can put a whole problem on it.
table.iri: Tables get used for everything that isn’t eating. Stitches. Charts. Waiting.
table.nova: There’s a scratch under the edge shaped like a seven. Not mine.
table.bob: The table has no sensors. What happens at it is mostly unknown to me, which seems correct.

bench.quenby: Too narrow to sleep on. People try.
bench.iri: The edges catch. I know where.
bench.nova: Left end: you can watch the hatch and the corridor light at the same time.
bench.bob: I hear the bench through the deck when it takes weight. I do not know who sits on it unless they speak.

cabinet.quenby: Spoons in the drawer. Bolts in the mug. Don’t ask me which is the joke.
cabinet.iri: I left the bolts where they were. Some things are filed by whoever found them first.
cabinet.nova: The door sticks on the first pull and gives on the second.
cabinet.bob: This cabinet has no latch sensor. I know it opens only because the sound carries.

fan.quenby: It ticks once and gives up. I know the feeling.
fan.iri: It ticks when the air cycle starts. I hear it from the corridor and know the galley air is turning over.
fan.nova: Tick. Then a long nothing. Then the air smells newer.
fan.bob: Corner fan, domestic loop. It ticks at start-up. I have logged the tick as a fault twice and withdrawn it twice.
